hints: Focus on what average rate means here, it is simply the volume of hydrogen made in that time interval divided by the time taken.
Work out P first from the table, the volume goes from 0 to 64 cm3 in the first 30 s, so divide 64 by 30.
Now find Q from the last 30 s change from 150 s to 180 s, then subtract this small late rate from the fast early rate.
walkthrough:
**Recall the rule for average rate**

Think of rate as how fast the gas volume grows. For any interval:

$$\text{average rate} = \frac{\text{change in volume of } \text{H}_2}{\text{time taken}}$$
Units will be $\text{cm}^3 \text{s}^{-1}$.

**Calculate P for the first 30 seconds**

From 0 s to 30 s, volume changes from 0 to 64 $\text{cm}^3$.

$$P = \frac{64 - 0}{30} = \frac{64}{30} = 2.13 \text{ cm}^3 \text{s}^{-1} \text{ (to 3 s.f.)}$$
This is fast because reactants are at maximum concentration.

**Calculate Q for the last 30 seconds**

From 150 s to 180 s, volume changes from 161 to 167 $\text{cm}^3$. Only 6 $\text{cm}^3$ is made.

$$Q = \frac{167 - 161}{30} = \frac{6}{30} = 0.20 \text{ cm}^3 \text{s}^{-1}$$
This is slow because metal is used up and acid is more dilute, so collisions are less frequent.

**Find P minus Q**

Now subtract the slow late rate from the fast early rate:

$$P - Q = 2.133... - 0.20 = 1.933... \approx 1.93 \text{ cm}^3 \text{s}^{-1}$$
This matches the large drop in rate as the reaction slows down.

options.A: Incorrect. 1.21 cm3 s-1 is too low. It comes from misreading the table, for example using the wrong volume change for one of the intervals instead of 64 cm3 for the first 30 s and 6 cm3 for the last 30 s.
options.B: Correct. P = 64/30 = 2.13 cm3 s-1 and Q = 6/30 = 0.20 cm3 s-1, so P - Q = 1.93 cm3 s-1. This shows the expected slowing of rate with time.
options.C: Incorrect. 2.13 cm3 s-1 is just the value of P alone. The trap is to calculate the first rate correctly but forget to calculate Q and subtract it.
options.D: Incorrect. 3.43 cm3 s-1 is too high. It comes from combining volumes or times incorrectly, for example adding rates or dividing by the wrong time interval, rather than doing P minus Q.
